newsitem.title: UK: UK funds to buy gilts, sell UK shares - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK funds to buy gilts, sell UK shares - survey.

text.p: UK fund managers swung to a more positive view on British government gilts this month but remained mostly negative on UK equities, according to a survey by Merrill Lynch.
With recent sterling strength seen bearing down on UK inflation, Merrill said fund managers planned to increase their gilt holdings yet continued to be net sellers of domestic shares.

Merrill's survey, which tapped the views of 76 institutions managing funds totalling $1.9 billion, found a "positive balance" of 12 percent of those questioned planned to up their gilt holdings, up from a negative one percent the month before.
The balance in the Merrill poll is calculated by subtracting those planning to increase their holdings of a particular asset class from those planning a decrease.
Conversely a balance of 5 percent planned to cut their holdings of UK stocks, compared with one percent planning a reduction in the January poll.

"In the UK managers seem to prefer gilts over equities," said Merrill strategist Bijal Shah. "Few managers are pessimistic on the inflation outlook following recent sterling strength and this is seen to be improving the outlook for gilts."
However Shah said managers were still expecting higher UK rates and this was deterring them from buying UK equities, a stance he took issue with.
"In our view, UK equities are likely to outperform gilts because strong growth in the domestic and global economy should lift corporate profits," the Merrill strategist said.

Elsewhere fund managers stayed negative on U.S. shares, with the negative balance rising to 14 percent from 10 percent last month, but continued to add to their European equity holdings, with a positive balance of 12 percent compared with 11 percent.
They swung to a positive balance of 13 percent on Japanese equities from a negative three percent in January.

Those expecting a rising inflation rate over the next 12 months dipped to 76 percent from 82 percent, yet those expecting a rise in interest rates was little changed at 99 percent, compared with 100 percent a month earlier.
UK GDP was seen expanding 3.3 percent in 1997, from 3.4 percent in Januaru, while inflation through the year was expected to be 3.2 percent, down from 3.3 percent.
The poll was carried out between February 3 and 5.
